title: Keel's USDS mint limit is a revolving credit line: burning restores mint capacity up to the maximum
content:
The two vault functions are described as exact inverses. `mintUSDS` (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.2.1.2.1.1.1): the contract "will ensure the `RateLimits` allow for minting the required amount," then "reduce the Rate Limit by the amount of USDS minted," mint into the buffer and transfer to the Proxy. `burnUSDS` (…1.2.1): the contract "will increase the available Rate Limit for minting USDS by the amount of USDS being burned. This increase will be limited by the `maxAmount` parameter in the `Rate Limit` contract," then burn from the buffer and "`wipe` an equivalent amount from the vault's debt."

So the mint rate limit is not a lifetime issuance quota; it is available headroom on a revolving facility. Repaying debt restores borrowing capacity immediately, which is why burning can be Unlimited without weakening the constraint — every burn is simultaneously a risk reduction and a credit restoration.

The `maxAmount` ceiling on the restoration is the necessary guard. Without it, a large burn could push available capacity above the configured maximum and let a subsequent mint exceed the intended exposure; capping the refill keeps the limit an invariant rather than a running balance that history can inflate.

The combined effect is that the limit tracks what matters prudentially — how much USDS debt Keel has outstanding right now — rather than how busy it has been.
description: mintUSDS decrements the rate limit and burnUSDS increments it, capped by maxAmount — so the limit measures outstanding debt rather than cumulative issuance.
